faq.title: Lapland Bars, Questions & Answers
faq.sub: What visitors ask before a night out in Finnish Lapland.

items.q: What is an ice bar in Lapland?
items.a: An ice bar is a bar built from snow and blocks of lake ice, with the counter, walls and even the glasses carved from ice. It runs at roughly −5 °C inside, so venues like the Ice Bar at Arctic SnowHotel near Rovaniemi lend you a thermal cape or suit at the door. Each one is rebuilt with a new design every winter and melts away in spring, so it only exists from about December to April.

items.q: Where are the best après-ski bars in Levi and Ylläs?
items.a: In Levi, Hullu Poro Areena sits at the base of the main slope and holds up to 1,700 people across two floors, with ten bars and live Finnish acts; Bar Ihku and Pub Hölmölä take over later on. On the Ylläs side, Selvä Pyy in Äkäslompolo village is where everyone gathers after a day on the fells, and the nightclub at Lapland Hotels Äkäshotelli takes over once the pubs wind down. The lifts close around 4pm and the bars fill straight after.

items.q: Can you drink alcohol outdoors in Finland?
items.a: Broadly yes, with a caveat. Finland’s Public Order Act bans drinking in public places, but it explicitly exempts parks and comparable public areas as long as you are not obstructing others or causing a nuisance. Municipalities can still restrict specific spots such as town squares or playgrounds, and being drunk and disorderly in public is an offence. The legal drinking age is 18 for beer, wine and cider, and 20 for spirits.

items.q: What are typical bar opening hours in Lapland?
items.a: Most pubs open in the afternoon and serve until around midnight on weekdays, with later closing (often 2am or 4am) on Fridays and Saturdays in the ski resorts. Licensing law allows alcohol sales until 1.30am, with an extension permit needed to serve later. Hours shift with the season: resort bars run long during the winter ski months and keep shorter hours in the quiet shoulder seasons, so it is worth checking the venue directly before you set out.

items.q: What local drinks should I try in Lapland?
items.a: Look for lakka, a cloudberry liqueur made from the amber Arctic berry that ripens for only a few weeks each summer, often served chilled or stirred into a cocktail. Local craft beer is worth seeking out too: Lapland Brewery in Rovaniemi and Tornion Panimo in Tornio both brew with Arctic water. For something classic, Lapin Kulta was founded in Tornio in 1873, though its production moved to Lahti in 2010, and Koskenkorva is the everyday Finnish grain spirit.

items.q: Where can you buy alcohol in Finland outside bars?
items.a: Supermarkets and convenience shops sell fermented drinks such as beer, cider and low-alcohol wine up to 8.0% ABV, and drinks made any other way, such as spirit-based mixers, up to 5.5% ABV, usually until 9pm. Anything stronger, meaning spirits, stronger wines and beers above 8%, is sold only at Alko, the state-run chain, which keeps daytime hours and closes early on Saturdays. Most Alko stores are closed on Sundays, though some branches have opened on Sundays since the summer of 2026, so check the hours of your nearest one. In smaller Lapland villages the nearest Alko can be some distance away, so it is worth stocking up before heading out to a remote cabin.

cityVibes.Rovaniemi: The Arctic capital after dark, craft brewery pubs, cocktail bars, and an actual bar made of ice.
cityVibes.Levi: Finland's après-ski capital. Hullu Poro Areena holds 1,700 people. The slopes close at 4pm and the party starts at 4.01pm.
cityVibes.Yllas: Quieter than Levi, warmer than anywhere. Cosy fell pubs where locals and visitors mix without pretension.
cityVibes.Saariselka: Remote, dark, and surprisingly well-stocked. Gastropub Giitu keeps a craft beer list worth the trip this far north.
cityVibes.Ruka: Kuusamo's fell resort in Koillismaa, not in Lapland. Thirteen venues at the resort itself: slope bars, an ice bar, a bowling-alley bar and two night clubs.
cityVibes.Pyha: Six venues in a compact fell resort: slope pubs, a wine bar and a sports bar. Several of them run winter hours only.
cityVibes.Luosto: Seven venues around one hotel village: hotel bars, a hut cafe-bar at the end of Kerotie, and a log restaurant whose public nights are ticketed dances with live orchestras.
cityVibes.Salla: Four venues: a log restaurant at the foot of the slopes, an apres-ski pub, and karaoke at the other two.
cityVibes.Iso-Syote: On the Syöte fells in Pudasjärvi, not in Lapland. Five venues: a pub, an after-ski bistro, a bar at the summit and a wine restaurant.

Café & Bar 21.description: Rovakatu 21, right in the heart of Rovaniemi. The most consistently mentioned bar in the city, a hybrid café by day, cocktail bar by night. Creative drinks, curated wine list, a refined crowd. A favourite of locals and visitors who want something beyond a standard pub.

Uitto Pub.description: A legendary Rovaniemi institution. "Comfortable, relaxed, and legendary", Uitto has been serving locals high-quality beers, drinks, snacks and meals for decades. No pretension, just a good Finnish pub doing what a good Finnish pub should do.

Nook Lounge.description: A cosy café-bar hybrid where good drinks are made slowly and conversations run long. The bartenders know what they are doing. Popular with travellers who have been on their feet all day and want somewhere warm, unhurried, and properly lit.

Bull Bar & Grill.description: In the Arctic City Hotel building, this American-style grill bar has a lively evening atmosphere. Good burgers, proper drinks, sports on screen. The kind of place that fills up after 9 and stays loud until late.

Ice Bar @ Arctic SnowHotel.description: Built from scratch every winter, this ice bar is carved by artists and rebuilt with a new theme each season. Located at the Arctic SnowHotel on Lake Lehtojärvi, 30 minutes from Rovaniemi city centre. Drinks served in glasses made of ice. Temperature: −5 °C inside. Thermal suits provided.

tour.label: Ice bar visit + thermal suit
tour.hint: Guided SnowHotel visit, including Ice Bar access.

Hullu Poro Areena.description: Levi's big room, at the foot of the main slope. Up to 1,700 people across two floors, ten bars and a large dance floor. Finnish headliners and DJs through the ski season. It has been running since 2001.

Bar Ihku.description: Already a legend among Levi party-goers. Ihku has accumulated stories over years of late-night Lapland chaos. Karaoke, dancing, Finnish locals and international skiers sharing the same floor. One of those places that looks ordinary until 11pm — then you understand why everyone talks about it.

Pub Hölmölä.description: "Levi's funniest pub." Hölmölä offers the best brewery products and cocktails, followed by unpretentious bar food. Board games, table football and billiards available free of charge. The kind of pub that doesn't take itself seriously, which is exactly what makes it great.

Bar Alakerta.description: Sunny terrace, live music and the legendary Open Stage Jams on Sundays. Alakerta attracts musicians and music lovers, both locals and visiting artists who have heard about the Sunday sessions. Unpretentious, warm, with the kind of atmosphere that happens when people actually love what they are doing.

Pub Old Mates.description: A proper British-style pub dropped into the middle of Finnish Lapland. Old Mates does pints properly, shows football, and provides a corner of familiar comfort for those who need it after a long day on the slopes. Better than most pubs in Britain, because Finnish beer is actually good.

Selvä Pyy.description: The go-to pub in Äkäslompolo village on the Ylläs side. Selvä Pyy serves craft beers, cocktails and proper Finnish pub food in a warm, log-cabin atmosphere. After a day on the fells, this is where locals and skiers converge — no pretension, just good drinks and easy company.

Pirtukellari Night Club.description: The nightclub at Lapland Hotels Äkäshotelli, in the same building as the Pirtukirkko restaurant. When the pubs wind down, the party moves downstairs: DJs, dancing, and a floor that fills fast in peak season.

Gastropub Giitu.description: The best bar in Saariselkä, a proper gastropub with an impressive craft beer selection and a menu that goes well beyond pub basics. Giitu serves Lapland-inspired dishes alongside a rotating tap list. The atmosphere is warm, modern, and exactly what you want after a Northern Lights hunt.

Lapland Brewery.description: Rovaniemi's own brewery, out on Teollisuustie a short drive from the centre rather than in town. Beers are brewed on site and poured in the taproom beside the tanks. The brewery describes itself as Finland's northernmost. The Friday tour and tasting needs booking in advance.

tour.label: Brewery tour & tasting
tour.hint: Register by Wed 14:00, minimum 3 people. Reserve via info@lapinpanimo.fi or +358 45 133 4410.

Public House Sohva.description: A warm and helpful beer restaurant along Levi's main street. Sohva is the kind of place you walk into planning one drink and leave three hours later. Good beer selection, decent food, friendly service. The daytime crowd flows straight into the evening one.

Bar Ihku Ruka.description: A karaoke bar, night club and after-ski venue inside the Scandic Rukahovi hotel in Ruka village. The slope bar and terrace open in the afternoon, karaoke runs nightly and the night club opens on Friday and Saturday. The venue also runs weekly trivia and bingo nights and takes table reservations.

Ravintola Zone.type: Night club and live music restaurant
Ravintola Zone.description: A restaurant in Ruka village that serves breakfast, lunch and grill food by day and becomes a music and dance venue at night. Its own site says it hosts over 100 live nights a year, from established Finnish artists to newer acts, and karaoke starts at 21 every night. There is a rooftop Panorama Terrace that can be booked privately.

Rinneravintola Piste.description: A slope restaurant and bar at the foot of Ruka's front slopes, described by its own site as serving cold drinks, hot drinks and food. Ruka's Spring Break site calls it the resort's party institution and landmark, with music all day and a terrace looking over the slopes and the spring pond-skim events.
highlights: At the foot of the front slopes

Hanki Baari.description: A bar and restaurant in Ruka village that calls itself 'your local living room in the arctic'. Its own site lists local beers, craft drinks, wines and coffee alongside simple food, and it runs a rotating calendar of live artists and DJs through the winter, from folk to alternative. Dogs are welcome and it does not take table reservations.

Lobby Bar Scandic Rukahovi.description: The lobby bar of the Scandic Rukahovi hotel in the centre of Ruka village. The hotel's own page describes it as a cosy spot for refreshing drinks and small snacks with sports on the big screen. Café service starts at 7 in the morning and the bar runs until the small hours.

Restaurant Colorado Ruka.description: An American-style bar and grill in the walking centre of Ruka. Its own page pairs the food with 'rock music' and describes an attached bar with live music nearly every week during the ski season, games, billiards and a sun terrace. Meats are grilled in a charcoal oven and the burger patties are made in house.
highlights: Live music most weeks in ski season

Monomesta.description: A slope bar and terrace at the foot of the Pessari slopes in a sheltered valley, reachable only on skis with a valid lift ticket - there is no road access. Ruka's own sites call it a legendary terrace and describe an apres-ski terrace that takes up to a thousand guests, with live acts, DJs, several bars and side competitions during Spring Break. Day shows are free and the serving area is 18+.
highlights: Terrace for up to a thousand

Ski Booster.description: A bar, cafe and grill in the Vuosseli part of Ruka, registered as a pub and bar business under the company Ruka Booster Oy. It is closed at the start of the week and runs late on Friday and Saturday nights.

Rukan Salonki Ice Bar.description: A bar built entirely of ice at Rukan Salonki Chalets, by the lake outside Ruka village. It serves both hot and cold drinks - hot cocoa and steaming juice to warm up, or ice-cold cocktails and mocktails.

CAMP Kitchen & Bar.description: A restaurant and bar in the Vuosseli side of Ruka, in Ruka Valley. Its own site describes international food 'from Turku to Thailand, from Nuorgam to New York' served alongside drinks, and names the bar in its own title.
highlights: Bar named in the venue's own title

Rukan keilahalli.description: A bowling hall on the lowest floor of the Kumpare shopping centre in Ruka village, reached by the stairs between the info desk and Subway. Its own site says the bar has a wide selection of affordable drinks. There are also two pool tables and three dart boards.
highlights: Two pool tables and three dart boards

Rukan Olkkari.description: A cafe-restaurant in Ruka's Vuosseli area whose own tagline is 'From the slope straight to the sofa'. Its site lists hot drinks, savoury and sweet waffles, food, after-ski drinks and karaoke, and the venue also does catering. The menu includes burgers, vegetarian dishes, fries and starters. Pets are welcome.

Hotelli-ravintola Rukatonttu.description: A hotel restaurant with a glazed terrace on the shore of Lake Talvijärvi, 650 metres from Ruka village centre and about 20 metres from the nearest slope and ski track. The restaurant and terrace seat 120. Its own site has a 'Ravintola & baari' section and says after ski is spent by the fireplace in the restaurant.

TunturiPUB.description: Tunturi Pub sits under the front slopes of Iso-Syöte, a few dozen metres from KIDE Hotel, and shares premises with the Tunturi Market grocery shop — the company's own site calls it "samoissa tiloissa toimiva ravintola Tunturi Pub". The kitchen serves pizzas, burgers, salads and smaller snacks plus a separate children's menu, either eaten in or phoned ahead and collected. The ski resort's restaurant page lists cold draught drinks and vegan options, and the pub's own page says evenings can also be spent, with a licence, in what it calls wetter spirits. In the corner there is a pile of board games.
highlights: Shares premises with the Tunturi Market grocery shop

Bistoria Iso-Syöte.description: Bistoria is the restaurant attached to KIDE Hotel at the foot of the Iso-Syöte fell, serving breakfast and dinner alongside what its own site calls a relaxed bar for the evening; lunch is by advance reservation for groups. The kitchen pairs local ingredients with international, Italian-leaning dishes and lists meat, vegetarian and gluten-free options. The wine list runs by the glass and by the bottle, starting at EUR 8.80. The ski resort's restaurant page adds an outdoor terrace and a lounge area.
highlights: Wine by the glass from EUR 8.80

Pärjä Ski Bistro.description: Pärjä Ski Bistro stands right next to the lifts on Iso-Syöte's back slopes. Its own site bills the place as "Iso-Syötteen after ski taivas" — Iso-Syöte's after-ski heaven — and promises food, drink and entertainment. The menu is organised into burgers, pizza, international dishes, a children's list and desserts, with ribs and wings and vegan options per the ski resort's restaurant page. The terrace catches the spring evening sun.
highlights: Right next to the back-slope lifts

Ravintola Hilltop.description: A 200-seat panoramic restaurant on the top floor of the Hilltop Hotel at the summit of Iso-Syöte fell. The kitchen combines what it calls clean northern flavours with local ingredients — foraged mushrooms, berries and local reindeer. The same space runs as Cafe Hilltop between 10:30 and 18:00, and the destination listing's photo caption shows a bar and lobby area by the restaurant entrance.
highlights: 200 seats at the summit of the fell
Northern ingredients: foraged mushrooms, berries, reindeer
Cafe Hilltop 10:30-18 in the same room

Restaurant Kotva.description: A small Nordic-gastronomy restaurant on top of Pikku-Syöte fell, part of Ski Resort & Hotel Pikku-Syöte. Dishes are built around regional ingredients. The drinks list is what the restaurant calls a considered collection of surprising small-producer wines and Finnish beverages. Dinner only, on Fridays and Saturdays, and only during the season the venue announces.
highlights: Three courses EUR 59, five courses EUR 79

Hanki Baari Pyhä.description: Baari Pyhän Pohjoisrinteiden alapäässä. Oma sivu lupaa yksinkertaista ruokaa, juomia, paikallisia oluita, laadukkaita viinejä ja kahvia. Talvikaudella tapahtumakalenterissa on artisteja ja DJ:itä lähes joka viikonloppu, folkista ja suomiräpistä vaihtoehtomusiikkiin. Klo 21 jälkeen K-18, paitsi alaikäiset vanhemman seurassa; tapahtumaillat ovat aina K-18. Auki jälleen joulukuussa 2026.
highlights: Paikallisia oluita ja live-artisteja lähes joka viikonloppu talvikaudella

Mesta.description: A bar and terrace in the middle of the slopes next to Hotel Kultakero, with views over the Lapland landscape from sunrise to the northern lights. Pyhä's own tourist site lists it under Bar/After ski and Slope restaurant and describes flavours, music and views. A festival page on the same site places it at the far end of the Hotel Pyhätunturi parking area beside the Kultakero 2 building, and calls it a place to relax with refreshments and pub-style food.

Pyhä Dreams Wine Bar.description: Viinibaari Pyhä Dreams -maisemamökissä Pyhätunturin huipulla, jonne noustaan maisemahissillä. Kesäkausi kulkee 19.6.2026 alkaen syyskuun 20. päivään ja talvikausi marraskuun lopusta noin vappuun. Paikka järjestää myös opastetun viinimaistelun enintään kahdeksan hengen ryhmille: viisi valko-, puna- ja kuohuviiniä suolaisten ja makeiden suupalojen kanssa, kesto noin kaksi tuntia. Tilat ovat rajalliset, joten ennakkovaraus kannattaa.

CAMP Kitchen & Bar PYHÄ.description: A restaurant and bar next to Hotel Pyhätunturi, serving dishes the venue describes as running from Turku to Thailand and from Nuorgam to New York. Panoramic windows open onto the fell scenery, and Pyhä's tourist site notes you can stop by for a drink at the end of the day or stay for a full dinner. Dogs are welcome and table reservations and gift cards are available.

Restaurant Huttuhippu.description: A restaurant next to Pyhä's family slope that works as a ski slope restaurant during the day and an a la carte restaurant in the evening, with reindeer from nearby farms and berries and mushrooms from local forests. The adjoining Huttu-Pub is known for its craft brewery products and a wide range of beers, whiskies and rums; Pyhä's tourist site calls it the local pub with the largest beer selection in the resort. Bingo runs on Thursdays, and the pub has board games and views over the slopes.
highlights: Largest beer selection in the resort

Sport Bar Pyhä.description: A bar in the Pyhä shopping centre that the operator describes as a living-room-style place in the heart of the resort centre, open all year round from the afternoon until late. It has a pool table, pinball, a dartboard, air hockey and board games, plus karaoke ranging from evergreens to newer songs. The kitchen serves pub food from burgers to wings, also as take-away, and the Viaplay channel package covers sports broadcasts.

Papana Pupi.description: The house pub of Sallatunturin Tuvat at Sallatunturi, in the same building as the reception and Restaurant Kiela. Its own page says the drinks list runs from house signature cocktails and mocktails to beers and wines, many made using local producers' products, alongside espresso-based coffees. Winter weeks include karaoke, a music quiz and bingo, and changing live artists play at weekends. The walls carry match jerseys and sticks from Finnish ice hockey players, and the large terrace is pet-friendly.

Keloravintola.description: A log restaurant at the foot of the front slopes of Salla Ski Resort. Its own site says the restaurant is fully licensed and serves grilled food, pizza and a la carte dishes cooked from scratch using Lappish raw materials. Salla Ski Resort describes a sunny terrace and after-ski gatherings here, and Visit Salla and the 2025 Salla product manual add live music evenings.

Ravintola Sallan Maja.description: A restaurant and pub in Salla with a lunch and a la carte kitchen alongside its pub, Majan Pubi. The pub page says you can sing karaoke, play board games and have drinks in company into the early hours, and it states a K-18 age limit from 22:00 with ID on request. The kitchen uses regional Lapland ingredients and the pastries and pizza bases come from small local bakeries, including Kursulainen.
highlights: Karaoke and board games in Majan Pubi
K-18 from 22:00, ID checked on request
Mon-Thu lunch buffet EUR 13.50 including salad buffet and coffee

Evakko Pub.description: A pub at Kairalan Kievari in the village of Vallovaara, set in an old elementary school building. Visit Salla says it is open at weekends until the early hours when needed and has a varied live music offering. The venue's own page describes a game room with darts and billiards, and lists alcoholic drinks, coffee, soft drinks and hot chocolate. The Kairalan Kievari accommodation site calls it a popular karaoke pub and the local night spot.

Nightclub Karhu.description: Karhu is the nightclub at Lapland Hotels Luostotunturi and, on the hotel's own wording, the village's only nightclub. Karaoke plays in the evenings and on artist nights the parties continue into the small hours; in spring the dancing to orchestras and guest artists runs until 04.00. The autumn 2026 calendar lists karaoke on most evenings, two Ruska pub-quiz nights and live bands including PIENIsuuriBÄNDI and Toni Jaatinen Band.
highlights: The only nightclub in Luosto village, per the hotel's own site
Live bands 10 EUR on artist nights

Rumpu Bar (Rumpubaari).description: Rumpu Bar sits next to the à la carte restaurant Bistro at Lapland Hotels Luostotunturi. The hotel describes it as a place to enjoy a cup of something hot or a refreshing drink. Dogs are welcome in the bar.
highlights: Next to the hotel's à la carte restaurant Bistro
Open later than the Bistro kitchen

Restaurant Punakettu.description: Punakettu is a family restaurant in Luosto's shopping centre that its own English site describes as "a restaurant and a pub". The published drinks list carries draught beer, long drinks and ciders, a local craft brewery section, wines by the glass and bottle, a full cocktail and mocktail list with house creations, and Teerenpeli whiskies. The food side is burgers, pizzas and Lappish dishes, and the restaurant holds a Green Key certificate.
highlights: Own site calls it "a restaurant and a pub"
Local craft brewery section on the drinks list

Restaurant Vaisko.description: Vaisko is an Eat Lappi restaurant in Luosto built around local ingredients and forest produce. Its own page gives the drinks equal billing: a wine cabinet with pairings and social pours, a small selection of domestic and international beers, and a cocktail list of classics plus the house's own creations. The site states you are welcome at Vaisko just for a drink, and the loft upstairs seats about thirty for groups.
highlights: Own site invites guests in just for a drink

Aarnikota.description: Aarnikota calls itself a "Hut Café and Bar", a small traditional Laplander's hut in Aarniluosto about 1.5 km from Luosto centre, reachable on foot, on skis, on snowshoes or by car. During the day it serves crepes and black-pot coffee, and its own page says it offers beverages for adults as well as for children. The heart of the hut is an open fire pit that seats twenty; in the evening it opens by request for groups of up to twenty.
highlights: Calls itself a hut café and bar; serves drinks for adults
Reachable on foot, skis or snowshoes from the village

Restaurant Aurora.description: Restaurant Aurora is the restaurant of Santa's Hotel Aurora, within walking distance of Luosto village centre. It has an open kitchen with a lava stone grill, a fireplace and windows onto the forest, and the menu is built around traditional flavours, international influences and a selected wine list. The hotel lists a lobby bar among its dining services, and the restaurant page describes the lobby bar's softly lit atmosphere as a setting for relaxed conversation.
highlights: Lobby bar named on the hotel's own service list
Lava stone grill in an open kitchen

Keloravintola (Log Restaurant Kelo).description: Keloravintola is an atmospheric log restaurant about 300 metres from Lapland Hotels Luostotunturi, seating up to 220 diners. The hotel states it is open by reservation only apart from theme nights, and hosts weddings and birthdays as a function venue. Its public evenings are ticketed dances with live dance orchestras: the autumn 2026 calendar lists Toni Jaatinen Band, Alina Liikola & Afrodite, Marko Maunuksela & Fantasia, Tomi Markkola & Kipinä and Tanssiorkesteri Ässät. The hotel also names karaoke, live music and bingo here.
highlights: Ticketed dance evenings with live orchestras, 15-20 EUR

Local Pub Panimo Saariselkä.description: A pub in the centre of Saariselkä that calls itself "your living room in Saariselkä" and serves a local and international selection of drinks. The kitchen runs every day alongside the bar. The pub also has separate men's and women's saunas that guests can use during public hours or book privately.

Kaunis Jorma Saariselkä.description: A small pub in the centre of Saariselkä, in a building completed at the end of 2023, open all year. It has a fireplace, a terrace, karaoke and a drinks selection alongside pub food. Free bingo runs every Thursday at 19:00.

Kieppi Kitchen & Bar.description: The restaurant of Wilderness Hotel Kieppi in central Saariselkä, serving Lappish cuisine with modern touches. The à la carte menu covers steaks, local fish, burgers and pan pizzas. A bar corner serves drinks and opens several hours before the kitchen.

Lobby Bar Takka.description: The fireplace lobby bar at Lapland Hotels Riekonlinna, next to Restaurant Linnansali. It serves drinks and hot beverages, and dogs are welcome. In autumn and early spring troubadours play in the bar, with free entry.

Restaurant Pirtti.description: The pub in the restaurant building of Santa's Hotel Tunturi. The hotel describes it as a relaxed, cozy living room you drift into after a day outdoors, with a warm traditional Lapland pub atmosphere, wooden interiors, a fireplace and an after-ski spirit. Its own page leads with good drinks and simple comfort food. Lapland North notes it is open during high seasons only, and neither the hotel nor Lapland North publishes daily opening hours — check by phone before going.

Restaurant Siula.description: The dance restaurant in the restaurant building of Santa's Hotel Tunturi, described by the hotel as a legendary dance restaurant where music, laughter and dancing fill the evenings. During the winter season the same room serves breakfast in the morning.

Mettäbaari.description: A bar in the forest beside Saariselkä's fitness/ski trail, two kilometres towards Laanila, in a group of old log buildings the owners describe as having a colourful history. After a few quiet years new owners reopened it as Mettäbaari. It holds a full alcohol licence (A-oikeudet) and its own line is that you can step in straight off the ski track. The simple menu is pancakes, familiar soft and hot drinks and local delicacies such as smoked Lake Inari whitefish. Twice a year, in spring and autumn, the old horse stable is turned into a dance room for the Monotanssit ski-boot dances with live music, and singers can do karaoke between sets.
highlights: Step in straight off the ski trail, 2 km towards Laanila
Pancakes and smoked Lake Inari whitefish

Restaurant Kaunis.description: The restaurant of Star Arctic Hotel on the Kaunispää fell, serving Arctic cuisine built on reindeer, Lake Inari fish and arctic berries. Its fireplace Lounge Bar pours wines and house cocktails made with berries local to the area, which the hotel says are available only at this bar.

Northern Lights Lounge.description: On Wednesday and Saturday evenings through the dark season the Kaunispää summit restaurant runs as the Northern Lights Lounge. The bar serves cocktails, wines, beers, soft drinks and small bites, and guests watch for the aurora from the summit's outdoor viewing areas or from the warm indoor lounge. A ticket includes entrance, one warm drink and snacks, and a host for the evening; other drinks and food are bought on the spot. Return transfers from Saariselkä can be included in the ticket.
highlights: Aurora watching from the summit of Kaunispää
Cocktails, wines and beers at 438 m
Ticket includes a warm drink, snacks and a host

Igloo Bar.description: A bar inside the Aurora Restaurant in the West Village of Kakslauttanen Arctic Resort. It serves cocktails in a space that combines traditional log architecture with glass igloos and looks out over the surrounding landscape.

Piano Bar at East Village Restaurant.description: A bar within the East Village Restaurant at Kakslauttanen Arctic Resort, described by the resort as having live piano music. The East Village Restaurant itself is a kelo log restaurant and the main dining venue for that side of the resort.

Bistro & Café Kuukkeli.description: A café-restaurant in the Kuukkeli Shopping Center in the centre of Saariselkä. The venue's own page describes a fireplace bar where guests can have drinks. Food service covers breakfast, a weekday lunch buffet and pizzas, burgers, sautéed reindeer and soup.

Joiku Pub.description: Joiku Pub is the village pub in Äkäslompolo, run by the same company as the Eväskori pizzeria next door (both listed under business ID 3090445-7). Its own site calls it Ylläs's legendary evening venue: a relaxed room with good music, karaoke and a dance floor that fills late into the night. The village's largest sun terrace belongs to the pub and serves from early spring to late autumn, and outside the season there is a billiard table in the pub. Table reservations only for groups over 10.

Los Lompolos.description: A small bar in the centre of Äkäslompolo. Its own one-line description, carried verbatim by both the Ylläs tourist board and Visit Finland, reads: tiny bar fulfilled with crossover music, cocktails and food, come as you are.

Miilu Bar & Grill.description: Miilu Bar & Grill stands on the shore of Lake Ylläsjärvi as part of Miilu Resort. The open fire grill, burning the house's own charcoal embers, is the heart of the kitchen, and the venue's listing says it puts seasonal ingredients together with a selection of drinks. Large windows face the lake. It can be reached by car, on foot, on skis, by bike or by snowmobile.

Taiga Ylläs.description: Taiga Ylläs describes itself on its own site as a restaurant, pub and slope restaurant at the foot of the Ylläs Ski South slope in Ylläsjärvi, serving Lappish food, local drinks, live music and a relaxed après-ski atmosphere. The ski resort's own listing adds that Taiga Pub is built around a changing selection of beers and charcoal-grilled food, with live music on performer nights and stand-up gigs in the spring season. It is open year-round.

Y1 Ski Pub.description: Y1 Ski Pub is part of the Y1 restaurant world at Ylläs Ski Resort on the Äkäslompolo side, near the base of the Aurinko-Express chairlift at Aurinkokuru. Lapland Hotels calls it the restaurant that opens first and closes last, with a traditional, warm pub-like room, a fireplace to sit by during or after skiing, live performers through the season and a terrace. The kitchen serves bistro food such as burgers, pita breads and ramen soups alongside a wide selection of hot and cold drinks.

Takka bar.description: The lobby bar at Lapland Hotels Äkäshotelli, in the same building as and next to Restaurant Pirtukirkko. The hotel describes it as the place for its mountain pizzas, a coffee or a refreshing drink, and it runs a soup lunch from 12 to 15.

Ravintola Pirtukirkko.description: The restaurant at Lapland Hotels Äkäshotelli, known for its church-like exterior, serving northern flavours and classic dishes from breakfast through à la carte dinner, with a buffet in peak season. Its own page leads on the nightlife side: dances are held there during the autumn and early spring with a published performer calendar, and admission is included in the room rate. Pirtukellari Night Club is in the basement of the same building, and the upstairs Pirtun Parvi keeps going until the early hours on performer nights.

Bistro (Lapland Hotels Saaga).description: One of the three restaurants at Lapland Hotels Saaga in Ylläsjärvi, alongside the buffet restaurant Biegga and the à la carte Tsohka. The hotel's own page says that in the summer at the relaxed and cosy Bistro you can enjoy cocktails made by the bartender or a cold drink on the sunny terrace; the food is snack-style, such as salmon soup. The hotel sits next to the southern slopes of Ylläs, with the gondola right beside it.

Lobby Bar (Lapland Hotels Ylläskaltio).description: The bar next to the reception at Lapland Hotels Ylläskaltio in Äkäslompolo. The hotel says it serves refreshing drinks and hot drinks with a Snacks menu and that dogs are welcome, and the hotel's soup lunch is served here from 12 to 15. Dance events are held in the hotel's restaurant during the autumn and spring weeks, with admission included in the room rate.

Ski pub Ala-Asema.description: Ski pub Ala-Asema sits next to the lower station of the Ylläs gondola on the Ylläsjärvi side. The resort's slope-restaurant page and the venue's own listing describe a relaxed ski pub with billiards, darts, board games and karaoke, serving drinks and pub food. A terrace is in use in season.

Cafe & Bar Routa.description: Cafe & Bar Routa is a cafe and bar in the heart of Äkäslompolo, in the K-Market Jounin kauppa building. The Ylläs tourist board page describes it as a lively cafe in the busiest part of the village and gives a price range of 3–18 euros. It closes at 17, so it is a daytime spot rather than an evening bar.

Aurinkoravintola Ylläs.description: Aurinkoravintola is a traditional slope restaurant on the Aurinko slope on the Ylläsjärvi side of Ylläs, open during the ski season according to the lift timetables. The Ylläs tourist board page says it serves cold and hot drinks and food portions, and that its large terrace serves spring-winter sun seekers. Guests ski straight to the door.

Bistro Hissi.description: Bistro Hissi is at the foot of the slopes on the Ylläsjärvi side, by the Ylläs Express chairlift. Its own site says it serves pizzas, burgers, salads and snacks and is open when the lifts are running; the resort's slope-restaurant page adds that it serves warm and cold drinks by the fireplace. The same company also rents snowmobiles.

iceBars.title: Ice Bars in Finnish Lapland | LaplandBars
iceBars.description: Lapland's three ice bars: SnowVillage in Lainio, Arctic SnowHotel near Rovaniemi and Snowman World at Santa Claus Village. Seasons, prices, what to wear.

hero.title: Ice Bars
hero.sub: Built from snow and ice every winter. Melted every spring. Gone until next December. This is not a theme bar. It is a seasonal Arctic phenomenon.

intro: Every autumn, crews of ice artists and construction workers descend on the snow villages of Finnish Lapland. They cut blocks of ice from frozen lakes, pack tonnes of snow into moulds, and sculpt bars, chairs, arches and figures by hand. By December, the results are ready: fully functioning bars operating at -5°C, where every surface, the walls, the bar counter, the glasses, is made of ice.

Each year brings a new theme. The sculptures are never the same. What you experience in one winter will not exist in the next. That impermanence is the point. An ice bar is temporary by definition, and that is exactly what makes it worth experiencing before it is gone.

band.title: Don't just visit. Sleep in a snow room.
band.body: Snow suites at Arctic SnowHotel, Lainio Snow Village and Kakslauttanen rebuild every December. -5 °C inside, thermal-rated sleeping bag, breakfast in the warm restaurant. One night is plenty. You will remember it for years.

items.title: Temperature
items.body: Around -5°C inside. All ice bars provide thermal capes, suits or jackets included in the entry price. Dress in layers underneath.

items.title: Duration
items.body: Most visitors spend 20–45 minutes inside. Enough for 1–2 drinks and photos. Your fingers will tell you when it is time to leave.

items.title: Drinks
items.body: Classic cocktails, warm mulled wine, and Arctic-inspired specials. Served in cups or glasses made of ice, yes, you drink from ice.

items.title: Season
items.body: Open from approximately December to April, depending on temperatures. Some years are longer. Ice bars do not exist in summer.

SnowVillage IceBar.description: Carved entirely from snow and ice each winter by international ice artists. New theme and sculptures every season. Drinks served in glasses made of pure Arctic ice. Part of the Snow Village complex, combine it with a night in a snow suite.

Arctic SnowHotel IceBar.description: Located at Arctic SnowHotel on the shores of Lake Lehtojärvi. Rebuilt every winter with new artistic themes, carved by Finnish and international artists. Thermal suits provided. The lake setting makes this one of the most atmospheric ice bars in the world.
Arctic SnowHotel IceBar.stayHint: Snow rooms, glass igloos, log cabins

Snowman World Ice Bar.description: Inside the legendary Snowman World at Santa Claus Village, a different kind of ice bar experience, more family-friendly and accessible. Hot drinks and cold cocktails served amid snow sculptures. Good option if you are combining the ice bar with a Santa visit.
Snowman World Ice Bar.stayHint: Santa Holiday Village + Nova Skyland nearby

apresSki.title: Après-Ski in Lapland: Levi, Ylläs, Pyhä, Ruka, Salla, Luosto | LaplandBars
apresSki.description: Where the party starts when the lifts close: Levi, Ylläs, Pyhä, Ruka, Salla, Luosto, Iso-Syöte, Saariselkä.

hero.title: Après-Ski
hero.sub: In Lapland, the slopes close at 4pm and the party starts at 4:01. Finnish après-ski is louder, warmer, and more honest than anywhere else.

pillars.title: Slope-side
pillars.body: The best après-ski bars are literally at the base of the slopes. Ski to the door, skis on the rack, beer in hand.

pillars.title: Live music
pillars.body: Not DJs with laptops, actual bands. Finnish rock, folk, and pop performed in wooden venues with proper stage lighting.

pillars.title: Finnish spirit
pillars.body: No pretension. Finnish après-ski is for everyone: locals, tourists, families, groups. The atmosphere is the attraction.

stayHints.Levi: Slope-side at Hullu Poro, Levi Hotel Spa, K5 Levi.
stayHints.Yllas: Lapland Hotels Äkäshotelli, log cabins, ski-in/ski-out.
stayHints.Saariselka: Holiday Club Saariselkä, Santa's Hotel, glass igloos nearby.
stayHints.Pyha: Pyhä Igloos, Hotel Pyhätunturi, log chalets.
stayHints.Ruka: Scandic Rukahovi at the slope base, Rukan Salonki, ski-in cabins.
stayHints.Salla: Sallatunturin Tuvat, Holiday Club Salla, cabins by the slopes.
stayHints.Luosto: Lapland Hotels Luostotunturi, Luosto log cabins.
stayHints.IsoSyote: Hotel Iso-Syöte on the summit, KIDE hotel and cabins at the slope base.

Hullu Poro Areena.desc: The undisputed king. 1,700-capacity venue at the base of the front slope. Top Finnish artists, DJs and live bands nightly during ski season. The après-ski that other Lapland resorts aspire to.

Bar Ihku.desc: A Levi legend. Already full by 9pm and going strong at 2am. Karaoke, dancing, Finnish locals and international skiers, everyone ends up here eventually.

Bar Alakerta.desc: Open Stage Jams on Sundays. The après-ski for people who would rather listen to a guitarist than a DJ. Sunny terrace, proper atmosphere.

Pub Hölmölä.desc: "Levi's funniest pub." Board games, billiards, brewery beers, and bar food. The slow-down option after a big day on the slopes.

Selvä Pyy.desc: The go-to après-ski spot in Äkäslompolo village. Craft beers, cocktails, Finnish pub food in a log-cabin atmosphere. Finnish locals and resort visitors sharing the same space, warm, easy, unpretentious.

Pirtukellari Night Club.desc: The nightclub at Lapland Hotels Äkäshotelli, in the same building as the Pirtukirkko restaurant. When the pubs wind down, the party moves downstairs. Fri–Sat only, and peak season nights fill fast.

Hanki Baari Pyhä.desc: At the foot of the Northern slopes. Artists and DJs on most winter weekends. The Pyhä bar reopens for the season in December 2026.

Mesta.desc: In the middle of the slopes next to Hotel Kultakero, with a terrace over the piste.

Pyhä Dreams Wine Bar.desc: At the top of the Pyhä fell. A wine list rather than a dance floor.

CAMP Kitchen & Bar PYHÄ.desc: In the village next to Hotel Pyhätunturi. Restaurant 16–21, kitchen closes at 20:30.

Restaurant Huttuhippu.desc: Next to the family slope: a slope restaurant by day, à la carte and the Huttu-Pub in the evening. Open daily 13–22, kitchen until 21.

Sport Bar Pyhä.desc: In the Pyhä shopping centre. Karaoke, pool and darts, open 17–00 and until 02 at weekends.

Bar Ihku Ruka.desc: Ski-in at Scandic Rukahovi. Slope bar and terrace open at 14 every day, karaoke from 21, and the club runs until 04 on Friday and Saturday.

Ravintola Zone.desc: Open 08–04 every day, karaoke from 21 and more than a hundred live nights a year. There is a roof terrace.

Restaurant Colorado Ruka.desc: Live evenings almost every week through the ski season, a sun terrace and pool. Open 14–22, until 24 on Friday and Saturday.

Hanki Baari.desc: Village bar with food, artists and DJs through the winter. Open 11–18 on weekdays and later at the weekend.

Rinneravintola Piste.desc: Right at the foot of the front slopes. Open daily 11–18.

Lobby Bar Scandic Rukahovi.desc: In the ski-in ski-out hotel at the slope base, with sport on the screen.

Keloravintola.desc: At the foot of the family slopes with a sunny terrace. The ski resort's own site calls what happens here after-ski parties. Open daily 13–20.

Papana Pupi.desc: At Sallatunturin Tuvat, and the venue calls itself the heart of after-ski. Finnish rock musicians play here, dogs are welcome on the terrace, open 08–22 all year.

Rumpu Bar (Rumpubaari).desc: At Lapland Hotels Luostotunturi, an unhurried place for a drink or a coffee after the slopes.

Nightclub Karhu.desc: Luosto's late option at Lapland Hotels Luostotunturi, with guest artists and karaoke. Open Friday and Saturday 20–01.

Pärjä Ski Bistro.desc: By the back-slope lifts. The bistro's own page bills Iso-Syöte as an after-ski paradise, and in spring the terrace holds the afternoon sun.

TunturiPUB.desc: Right beside the front slopes next to the KIDE hotel. Open 12–00, until 03 on Friday and Saturday, kitchen to 21:30.

Restaurant Pirtti.desc: At Santa's Hotel Tunturi, about a kilometre from the slopes. In the restaurant's own words: good drinks, straightforward food and a cheerful after-ski mood.

north.title: Skiing further north?
north.sub: Saariselkä and Pyhä are quieter, more intimate après-ski destinations than Levi or Ylläs. Worth it for the smaller crowds and aurora-bar density.

cta.sub: Browse the full list of bars and pubs across all four destinations.

apresSki.notFound: Olos, Pallas and Suomu list slope restaurants on their own sites but name no bar, club or after-ski night. Kilpisjärvi has no downhill slopes at all.

cocktails.title: Lapland Cocktails: Cloudberry, Lingonberry | LaplandBars
cocktails.description: Three Arctic cocktails: Cloudberry Sour, Northern Lights and Lingonberry Spritz. The wild ingredients behind them and bookable tasting experiences.

hero.title: Arctic Cocktails
hero.sub: The same Arctic conditions that make Lapland's wild berries extraordinary make them exceptional in a glass. This is cocktail culture built on foraged ingredients you can't get anywhere else.

cocktails.ingredientsSub: Arctic conditions produce extreme ingredients, plants that develop higher concentrations of flavour and nutrients to survive the cold and the endless summer sun.

stayBand.title: Don't drive home, book a room nearby
stayBand.sub: Most of the best cocktail bars are in Rovaniemi, Levi or Saariselkä. Hotels with walking-distance access:

cocktails.name: Cloudberry Sour
cocktails.ingredients: Finnish gin · cloudberry liqueur · lemon juice · egg white · sugar syrup
cocktails.description: The signature Arctic cocktail. Cloudberries, the gold of the Arctic, ripen for just 2–3 weeks each July in subarctic bogs. Their honey-sweet tartness works perfectly in a sour. The egg white foam carries the scent of the fell straight to your nose.

cocktails.name: Northern Lights
cocktails.ingredients: Finnish vodka · blue curaçao · tonic water · edible shimmer · lime
cocktails.description: The show-off cocktail. Blue-green shimmer swirling in a glass, a deliberate tribute to the aurora borealis. Best ordered somewhere with a window facing north. The glitter settles in about 30 seconds; drink it before it does.

cocktails.name: Lingonberry Spritz
cocktails.ingredients: Prosecco · lingonberry juice · elderflower liqueur · soda water · fresh lingonberries
cocktails.description: Deep ruby-red, tart, refreshing. Wild Lapland lingonberries, Finland's most-picked berry, balance the floral elderflower against the bubbles. Simple but precisely right. The kind of drink that looks beautiful in a candlelit bar.

ingredients.name: Cloudberry (Lakka)
ingredients.note: The rarest Arctic berry, grows only in subarctic bogs, 2–3 weeks a year. Used in liqueur, sorbet, sour mixes.

ingredients.name: Lingonberry
ingredients.note: Finland's most beloved wild berry. Tart, earthy, versatile. Used in juice, liqueur, and garnishes.

ingredients.name: Birch Sap
ingredients.note: Collected in early spring when the sap runs. Clean, faintly sweet. Used in craft spirits and cocktail mixers.

ingredients.name: Arctic Thyme
ingredients.note: Foraged from fell meadows. More intense than cultivated thyme due to the extreme growing conditions.

ingredients.name: Sea Buckthorn
ingredients.note: Bright orange berries with more vitamin C per gram than oranges. Used in sours and shots.

ingredients.name: Finnish Gin
ingredients.note: Several Finnish distilleries produce gin infused with Arctic botanicals, birch, juniper, cloudberry, spruce tip.

craftBeer.title: Craft Beer in Lapland: Tornio & Rovaniemi | LaplandBars
craftBeer.description: Two Lapland breweries and their beers: Tornion Panimo on the Swedish border and Lapland Brewery's Rovaniemi taproom. Arctic beer styles and tastings.

hero.title: Craft Beer
hero.sub: Finnish craft beer is built on the same principles as Finnish food: pure water, wild local ingredients, and no shortcuts. The Arctic brings its own flavour to every pint.

tours.title: Brewery & food tours bookable now
tours.sub: Live availability from GetYourGuide. Brewery visits, distillery tastings and Lappish food experiences in Rovaniemi, Saariselkä and beyond.
tours.fallback: See all food & drink experiences in Lapland on GetYourGuide

stay.title: Skip the taxi, book a hotel within walking distance
stay.body: Tornion Panimo is across the river from town. Lapland Brewery sits on the Teollisuustie estate, a short drive out of central Rovaniemi. Pick the brewery, then book a hotel you can get back from easily.

breweries.name: Tornion Panimo
breweries.description: Brewing on the bank of the Tornionjoki began here in 1873. Hartwall closed the plant in 2010 and moved production south; in 2016 more than 1,900 small investors brought the brewery back through a crowdfunding campaign. It makes both beer and spirits, including Original Lapland Lager and Arctic Pale Ale, and runs tasting tours.

breweries.name: Lapland Brewery
breweries.description: Rovaniemi's own brewery, out on the Teollisuustie industrial estate rather than in the town centre. Beers are brewed on site and served in the taproom beside the tanks. The brewery describes itself as Finland's northernmost. Friday tours run through the winter and need booking ahead.

realBeers.title: Beers actually brewed up here
realBeers.sub: Every beer below is on its brewery’s own product list. Two breweries, both real: Lapland Brewery in Rovaniemi and Tornion Panimo on the Swedish border.

items.name: Hippu Lapland Golden Pilsner
items.desc: Bohemian-style pilsner, 4.3 %. The everyday pint at the taproom on Teollisuustie.

items.name: Saana Lapland Pale Ale
items.desc: Pale ale with a twist of juniper, 5.5 %, brewed at the Arctic Circle.

items.name: Hölmö IPA
items.desc: The brewery’s IPA at 5.4 %: the hoppy end of a range that is mostly lagers.

items.name: Loimu Savulager
items.desc: Smoked lager. Loimu is the Finnish word for the open flame that salmon is grilled beside.

items.name: Lapland Original Lager
items.desc: The flagship of the brewery that 1,900 small investors brought back in 2016. Lager, 5.2 %.

items.name: Routa Imperial Stout Bourbon Oaked
items.desc: Imperial stout aged on bourbon oak, 8.0 %. Routa means ground frost; this is the winter end of the list.

drinkingCulture.title: Finnish Drinking Culture in Lapland | LaplandBars
drinkingCulture.description: Koskenkorva, lonkero, Lapin Kulta, sauna beer and kalsarikännit: how Finns actually drink and what a pint costs in a Lapland bar.

hero.title: Finnish Drinking Culture
hero.sub: From Koskenkorva on a Friday night to kalsarikännit in your underwear, this is a guide to how Finns actually drink.

intro: Finnish drinking culture is built on contradictions. Finland has some of the strictest alcohol laws in Europe, state-controlled off-licences, limited pub hours, high taxes and some of the most enthusiastic drinkers. Alcohol here is not background noise. It is a deliberate act, taken seriously and often done with ceremony.

In Lapland specifically, drinking is inseparable from the environment. You drink after a day on the slopes, after a snowmobile tour, after a Northern Lights watch. The cold makes the warm drink better. The dark makes the candlelit pub cosier. The silence makes the laughter louder.

kossu.title: Koskenkorva, The National Spirit
body: If Finland has a national spirit, spiritually and literally, it is Koskenkorva. "Kossu" to anyone who knows it. A 38% ABV grain spirit distilled from Finnish barley in the village of Koskenkorva, Ostrobothnia, since 1953. The distillery runs 24 hours a day, every day of the year.

Koskenkorva is not vodka; it is specifically a grain spirit, with a slightly rougher, more characterful profile than filtered vodka. It is, however, extremely clean: distilled to a very high purity, with minimal congeners. The hangover, Finns will tell you, is almost nonexistent compared to cheaper spirits. This is either true or a very successful piece of Finnish mythology.

How do Finns drink it? Cold, straight, from a small glass. Sometimes with a beer chaser (the combination is called a viina + kalja, the classic Finnish working-class pairing). In Lapland, you will find it at every pub, usually on a speed rail. It has been on Finnish tables at weddings, funerals, Saturday saunas and Sunday breakfasts. It is not glamorous. That is the point.
kossu.facts: Produced by Altia (now Anora Group). Over 10 million litres sold annually in Finland. The village of Koskenkorva has a population of ~1,500 people. The distillery is one of the most efficient grain distilleries in the world, producing zero waste, the grain residue feeds livestock.

finlandia.title: Finlandia Vodka, Finland to the World
body: While Koskenkorva is for Finns, Finlandia is Finland's gift to the rest of the world. Launched in 1970, the same year as the first Earth Day, which is either a coincidence or a very deliberate piece of brand positioning, Finlandia was one of the first premium vodkas to market "purity" as its central selling point.

The recipe is simple by design: six-row barley grown in Finland, glacial spring water from Rajamäki, about 50 km north of Helsinki. The water is the star. Finnish glacial spring water is some of the softest in the world, low in minerals, low in hardness, which produces a distinctly clean, light vodka with virtually no aftertaste.

Finlandia is distilled over 200 times through a continuous distillation process, not batch-distilled like most premium spirits. The result is extremely consistent. It has won international blind tastings against much more expensive competitors. In Finland, it is still reasonably priced. Abroad, it wears its Finnish credentials as a badge of premium quality.
finlandia.facts: Owned by Coca-Cola HBC since 2023; before that it belonged to Brown-Forman (Jack Daniel's parent company). Available in over 80 countries. The iconic frosted bottle design has barely changed since 1970. Produced at the Rajamäki distillery, which has been making spirits since 1888.

lapinKulta.title: Lapin Kulta, Gold from the Arctic
body: If any beer truly belongs in a guide to Lapland bars, it is Lapin Kulta, literally "Lapland’s Gold." The brewery was founded in 1873 in Tornio, on the Finnish-Swedish border at the mouth of the Tornionjoki river, and the beer carried that Arctic address for well over a century. Hartwall closed the Tornio brewery in 2010 and moved production to Lahti, so the name still points north even though the brewing no longer happens here.

Lapin Kulta is Finland's classic pale lager, clean, light, malty, and uncomplicated. It will not win craft beer awards, and it does not try to. It is the beer that has been on Finnish cabin tables, sauna benches, and festival grounds for five generations. When Finns say "grab a beer," this is often the beer they mean. In Lapland specifically, ordering Lapin Kulta in a local pub feels right in a way no imported lager ever could.

The brand has changed corporate hands over the decades, today Hartwall and its parent Royal Unibrew own it, but the beer itself remains a Finnish staple. You will find it in every Lapland bar, every supermarket, every Alko. It is, in the best possible sense, completely ordinary.

prices.label: Draft pint in a Lapland bar
Craft beer pint in a Lapland bar

lapinKulta.priceFootnote: Prices approximate as of 2025. Supermarkets sell beer up to 8.0% ABV; anything stronger is sold only at Alko state liquor stores. The 5.5% ABV limit still applies to drinks not made by fermentation, such as spirit-based mixers.
lapinKulta.other: Karhu ("Bear"), Finland's best-selling beer, slightly maltier than Lapin Kulta. Sandels, named after a Finnish war hero, popular budget lager. Olvi, brewed in Iisalmi since 1878, the only major Finnish brewery still Finnish-owned. Koff, Helsinki's oldest brewery brand (1819), now owned by Sinebrychoff/Carlsberg.

lonkero.title: Lonkero, Born for the Olympics
body: In 1952, Helsinki hosted the Summer Olympics and visitors poured in from around the world, far more than the city's few licensed bars could ever mix drinks for. Alko, the state alcohol monopoly, turned to the Hartwall beverage company: what was needed was a ready-mixed drink that could legally be sold at the Olympic venues.

Hartwall's answer was the Original Long Drink: Finnish gin and grapefruit soda, 5.5% ABV. Light, crisp, slightly bitter. It was meant to be produced only for the Games, but the public had other plans: demand kept it in production after the Olympics ended. The lonkero was born.

Today lonkero is a cultural institution and an entire drinks category, still led by the grey-blue Original can. The category has spread far beyond Finland: in the United States, Finnish entrepreneurs turned the long drink into a brand of its own, making lonkero perhaps the most successful accidental export in the history of Finnish drinks.

brand.title: Hartwall Original Long Drink
facts: Created for the 1952 Helsinki Olympics, commissioned by state monopoly Alko
Finnish gin and grapefruit: the same recipe to this day, 5.5% ABV
The grey-blue can is a fixture of Finnish bars, terraces and sauna evenings

kalsarikannit.title: Kalsarikännit, The Art of Pants Drinking
body: There is a Finnish concept that has no direct equivalent in any other language: kalsarikännit. From kalsarit (underpants) and känni (being drunk). Literally: "pants drunk." The practice of getting drunk at home, alone or with close companions, in your underwear, with absolutely no intention of going out.

This is not a shameful thing in Finland. It is not considered antisocial. It is considered, by many Finns, to be the pinnacle of relaxation, a deliberate rejection of the social performance required by going to a bar. No getting dressed. No waiting for taxis. No small talk with strangers. Just your sofa, your drink of choice, and the freedom to watch whatever you want on television.

In 2015 the Finnish Foreign Ministry made Finland the first country in the world to publish its own emoji set, and kalsarikännit was in that original collection: a person in underwear with a drink. The campaign went viral globally. Finland was briefly the most discussed country in international news for a reason that had nothing to do with politics.

Kalsarikännit is not just a joke. It reflects something genuine about Finnish culture: the value of solitude, the comfort of one's own home, and a deep national suspicion of performative socialising. In Lapland, where winters are long, dark, and cold, kalsarikännit is practically a survival mechanism.
rules: 1. Put on the most comfortable underwear you own.
2. Stock the refrigerator before nightfall (this is non-negotiable).
4. Sit down. Do not stand up for at least two hours.
5. Drink slowly. This is not a race.
6. Do not, under any circumstances, make plans to go out later.
kalsarikannit.book: The idea even has its own book: Miska Rantanen’s Kalsarikänni (S&S, 2018), published in English the same year as Pantsdrunk by HarperCollins.

sauna.title: Sauna & Sisu, The Full Picture
body: Finnish drinking culture cannot be separated from the sauna. The standard Finnish Saturday follows a precise order: work, sauna, beer. The beer is consumed in the sauna or immediately after, when the body temperature is still high and the cold beer creates an almost physiological effect. This combination is so culturally embedded that most Finnish summer cottages have a dedicated sauna-beer ritual that begins at approximately 4pm and continues until someone falls asleep in the boat.

In Lapland, the sauna is even more central. After a day in -30°C, a sauna is not a luxury: it is rehydration, recovery, and socialising combined. Many Lapland hotels and cabins have private saunas. The combination of sauna, cold plunge into the lake or snow, and cold beer is, according to Finns, better than any spa treatment in the world. They are probably right.

Sisu, the uniquely Finnish concept of stoic determination, resilience in the face of adversity, applies to drinking too. A Finn who has been drinking for seven hours and still makes it to work on Monday is not considered irresponsible. They are considered to have sisu.

about.title: About LaplandBars
about.description: About LaplandBars, independent editorial about how and where Lapland drinks.
body: LaplandBars is an independent editorial guide to bars, pubs, ice bars and nightlife venues across Finnish Lapland, written from Finland, not generated from a database.

Every venue listed on this site is a real place; details are compiled from the venues' own pages and Google data. Coverage focuses on Rovaniemi, Levi, Ylläs and Saariselkä, the four main destinations in Finnish Lapland and listings are kept up to date as venues open, close and change. Sources are cited; corrections are welcome.
LaplandBars is part of the <1>LaplandVibes</1> ecosystem, a network of niche travel sites covering Finnish Lapland.
The site is operated by LaPeso Oy (Finland). Questions or corrections: <1>info@laplandvibes.com</1>

Some of the links on this site route through go.laplandvibes.com and earn a small commission when you book, at no extra cost to you. That income covers hosting and the time spent keeping the listings current. It does not decide which venues appear here: the commission comes from hotel and tour partners, not from the bars. Nothing on these pages is paid placement: no bar pays to be listed, and none pays for the editor's-pick badge.

What this is not: a booking platform. There is no live availability and no reservation system here. Each venue links to its own site, on purpose, because the venue is the only source that knows tonight's opening hours and whether the terrace is open. Treat the prices and hours on these pages as a starting point and confirm the rest at the door.

rovaniemi.name: Rovaniemi
rovaniemi.title: Bars in Rovaniemi: Pubs, Cocktails & the Ice Bar | LaplandBars
rovaniemi.description: Where to drink in Rovaniemi: centre pubs and cocktail bars a few streets apart, a brewery taproom and an ice bar 30 minutes out. Ratings, hours, prices.
rovaniemi.tagline: The only town in Lapland where you can choose a bar on foot.
rovaniemi.intro: Rovaniemi’s bars sit in a tight grid between Rovakatu, Koskikatu, Korkalonkatu and Maakuntakatu, so a night here is a walk, not a taxi ride. Café & Bar 21 on Rovakatu is the cocktail room the whole town mentions, Uitto Pub on Korkalonkatu is the old institution, Kauppayhtiö on Valtakatu mixes beer with live music, and Roy Club on Maakuntakatu takes over after everything else closes. Two are worth leaving the centre for: Lapland Brewery pours its own beer beside the tanks on Teollisuustie, and the Ice Bar at Arctic SnowHotel in Sinettä, about 30 minutes away, is rebuilt from ice every December.
know: Most of the bars are in the city centre within a few hundred metres of each other; Lapland Brewery, Pub Sarvi and the ice bar are outside it and need a car or a taxi.
The Ice Bar at Arctic SnowHotel is open daily 11–22 from mid-December to the end of March and needs a SnowHotel entrance ticket unless you stay overnight.
Lapland Brewery runs a brewery tour and tasting on Fridays at 17:00 in winter; register by Wednesday, minimum three people.

levi.name: Levi
levi.title: Bars in Levi: Après-Ski, Pubs & Late Nights | LaplandBars
levi.description: Where to drink in Levi: Hullu Poro Areena, Bar Ihku and the village pubs at the foot of the slopes, plus a fell-top restaurant. Ratings, hours, prices.
levi.tagline: Finland’s après-ski capital. The lifts stop at 16:00 and the bars fill straight after.
levi.intro: Levi’s bars are packed into the village at the foot of the front slope, officially called Sirkka, which is why the postal addresses say Sirkka or Kittilä. Hullu Poro Areena on Hissitie is the big room: two floors, ten bars and up to 1,700 people on concert nights. Bar Ihku on Keskuskuja and Pub Hölmölä on Hiihtäjänkuja carry the late shift, Public House Sohva and Pub Old Mates do beer and football, and Bar Alakerta on Myllyjoentie runs open-stage jams on Sundays. Restaurant Tuikku is the exception: it sits on the summit and hosts the afternoon après-ski when the ski season is on.
know: Everything except Tuikku is within walking distance in the village; the summit is reached by gondola, on skis or by the summit road.
Concert nights at Hullu Poro Areena are ticketed, usually around 25–30 euros; ordinary pub nights are free to enter.
V’inkkari and the après-ski venues run full hours only in the ski season, so outside winter check the venue before you plan the evening around it.

yllas.name: Ylläs
yllas.title: Bars in Ylläs: Äkäslompolo, Ylläsjärvi & Slope Pubs | LaplandBars
yllas.description: Where to drink in Ylläs: village pubs and a basement nightclub in Äkäslompolo, slope restaurants on both sides, a lakeside grill in Ylläsjärvi.
yllas.tagline: Two bar villages, Äkäslompolo and Ylläsjärvi, with slope pubs on both sides: the address tells you which list is yours.
yllas.intro: Ylläs has two bar villages and the address tells you which side you are on. In Äkäslompolo, Selvä Pyy at Tunturintie 16 is the pub locals and skiers use, Joiku Pub on Jakolantie has the village's largest sun terrace and a karaoke floor, and Los Lompolos on Sivulantie is the small cocktail room in the centre. Three venues share one address at Äkäsentie 10: Ravintola Pirtukirkko, the Takka bar beside it and Pirtukellari Night Club downstairs. Y1 Ski Pub at Tunturintie 56 is on the same side, near the base of the Aurinko-Express chairlift at Aurinkokuru. In Ylläsjärvi, Ski pub Ala-Asema and Bistro Hissi both sit at Iso-Ylläksentie 44, next to the gondola's lower station and the Ylläs Express chairlift, with the Bistro at Lapland Hotels Saaga at number 42. Bar Kaappi and Taiga Ylläs share Vaeltajantie 2 at the foot of the Ylläs Ski South slope, and Miilu Bar & Grill stands on the shore of Lake Ylläsjärvi as part of Miilu Resort.
know: The bars split between two villages: Äkäslompolo, postcode 95970, and Ylläsjärvi, postcode 95980. Miilu Bar & Grill is out on the shore of Lake Ylläsjärvi at Rantasaarentie 3-5, and its listing names car, foot, skis, bike and snowmobile as ways to get there.

Two places run on the lift timetable: Aurinkoravintola on the Aurinko slope is open during the ski season according to the lift timetables, and Bistro Hissi is open when the lifts are running. Pirtukellari Night Club opens in ski season on Friday and Saturday nights, and Y1 Ski Pub at Aurinkokuru opens in November 2026.

Restaurant services at Lapland Hotels Äkäshotelli, which cover Ravintola Pirtukirkko and the Takka bar, are closed from 27 September to 20 November 2026. At Lapland Hotels Saaga the hotel's own pages disagree: the Bistro's hours are marked until 26 September, while the seasonal notice says the restaurants are closed from 24 September to 14 November. Cafe & Bar Routa in Äkäslompolo is open all year but closes at 17, so it is a daytime stop rather than an evening one.

saariselka.name: Saariselkä
saariselka.title: Bars in Saariselkä: Village Pubs, Dances & a Summit Lounge | LaplandBars
saariselka.description: Where to drink in Saariselkä: pubs in the village centre, a gastropub, a dance restaurant, and an aurora lounge on the Kaunispää summit.
saariselka.tagline: Most of the drinking is on a handful of village streets, with one bar at the summit of Kaunispää and one out on the ski trail.
saariselka.intro: Saariselkä keeps most of its bars in a few village streets. Gastropub Giitu on Revontulentie pours craft beer daily until 02, with the kitchen on until 22. Teerenpesä on Saariseläntie is three venues under one log roof: a Lappish restaurant, a sports pub with darts and pool, and a nightclub running couples’ dances and a disco floor. Further along the same street, Local Pub Panimo at number 10 has its own men’s and women’s saunas, and Lobby Bar Takka at number 13 is the fireplace bar at Lapland Hotels Riekonlinna. Kaunis Jorma on Kiveliöntie runs karaoke and free bingo on Thursdays at 19:00, Kieppi Kitchen & Bar on Raitopolku opens its bar corner several hours before the kitchen, and Restaurant Pirtti and the dance restaurant Siula share the restaurant building at Santa’s Hotel Tunturi on Lutontie. Two more sit up on Kaunispää: Restaurant Kaunis at Star Arctic Hotel, and the summit restaurant that becomes the Northern Lights Lounge.
know: The venues sit on five village streets: Saariseläntie, Revontulentie, Kiveliöntie, Raitopolku and Lutontie. Teerenpesä, Local Pub Panimo, Kaunis Jorma, Kieppi and Bistro & Café Kuukkeli each describe themselves as being in the centre of Saariselkä. Mettäbaari is the exception: it is 2 km out towards Laanila and you step in straight off the ski trail.

The Northern Lights Lounge runs at the Kaunispää summit restaurant on Wednesday and Saturday evenings through the dark season, on a ticket that includes entrance, one warm drink, snacks and a host. Return transfers from Saariselkä can be added to the ticket.

Several venues publish no daily hours: Restaurant Pirtti at Santa’s Hotel Tunturi opens in high seasons only, and Restaurant Kaunis at Star Arctic Hotel is closed from 20 April to 29 October 2026. The two Kakslauttanen bars, Igloo Bar and the Piano Bar, sit outside the village on Kiilopääntie.

ruka.name: Ruka
ruka.title: Bars in Ruka: Slope Bars, Karaoke & Live Music | LaplandBars
ruka.description: Where to drink in Ruka: karaoke and live music on Rukankyläntie, a slope bar reached only on skis and a hotel restaurant bar out on the lake shore.
ruka.tagline: Six of these venues stand on one street, Rukankyläntie, and one more has no road to it at all.
ruka.intro: Ruka’s bar street is Rukankyläntie, in Kuusamo, and six venues carry its address. Restaurant Colorado sits at number 6 in the walking centre with billiards and a sun terrace, Hanki Baari at 11 pours local beers and books live artists and DJs through the winter, Ravintola Zone at 13 says it hosts over 100 live nights a year and keeps the grill on until 04, and Scandic Rukahovi at 15 holds two rooms: the Lobby Bar and Bar Ihku, the karaoke bar and night club. Rinneravintola Piste stands at number 17, at the foot of the front slopes. Vuosseli is the other named part of Ruka, and three venues place themselves in it: Ski Booster on Ahon Jussintie, CAMP Kitchen & Bar on Bistrotie and Rukan Olkkari on Jussinkuja. Four sit outside both: Rukatonttu, 650 metres from the village centre on Lake Talvijärvi; Monomesta, a terrace below the Pessari slopes with no road to it; Rukan Salonki Ice Bar on Salongintie; and Rukan keilahalli on Rukatunturintie.
know: Monomesta has no road access: you reach the terrace at the foot of the Pessari slopes on skis with a valid lift ticket, the day shows are free and the serving area is 18+. Rukan Salonki Ice Bar is out at the chalets by the lake on Salongintie, not in the village.

Some nights are ticketed. Bar Ihku takes door tickets from 8 euros and 10–25 euros on artist nights, Hanki Baari’s gigs usually run 10–15 euros, and live music at Restaurant Colorado is free to enter.

Ski Booster and Rukan keilahalli are both closed on Mondays and Tuesdays, and the bowling hall on Sundays as well; Rukatonttu serves Tuesday to Saturday 17–21. CAMP Kitchen & Bar is shut from 19 October to 17 November 2026 for a kitchen renovation and reopens daily 11–21 on 19 November.

luosto.name: Luosto
luosto.title: Bars in Luosto: One Nightclub, Dance Nights & a Hut Bar | LaplandBars
luosto.description: Where to drink in Luosto: the hotel nightclub and Rumpu Bar on Luostontie, a pub in the shopping centre, a hut bar and ticketed dance nights.
luosto.tagline: The village has one nightclub, and the live dance orchestras play in a log restaurant about 300 metres from Lapland Hotels Luostotunturi.
luosto.intro: Seven places in Luosto serve drinks. Lapland Hotels Luostotunturi at Luostontie 1 holds two venues: Nightclub Karhu, which the hotel calls the village's only nightclub, and Rumpu Bar, next to the Bistro restaurant and open to dogs. Keloravintola, the log restaurant seating 220, stands about 300 metres from the same hotel and opens to the public for ticketed dance evenings with live orchestras. Restaurant Punakettu at Luostontie 4 is in the shopping centre and calls itself a restaurant and a pub, with a local craft brewery section and Teerenpeli whiskies on the list. Restaurant Aurora at Luppokeino 1 belongs to Santa's Hotel Aurora, within walking distance of the village centre, and the hotel names a lobby bar among its dining services. Restaurant Vaisko at Hartsutie 1 welcomes guests in for a drink alone. Aarnikota sits apart: a Laplander's hut at Kerotie 10 in Aarniluosto, about 1.5 km from the centre, reachable on foot, on skis, on snowshoes or by car.
know: Vaisko is closed between seasons and opens for 2026–2027 on 26 November. Aarnikota publishes dated windows instead of a standing timetable; the current one is Wednesday to Sunday 11–16 for the ruska season, to 27 September 2026.

Karhu's karaoke is free of charge and K-18, live-band nights there are 10 euros, and Keloravintola's public dance evenings are ticketed at 15–20 euros. The 3-euro cloakroom fee is not included in the ticket price.

None of the seven publishes standing weekly opening hours: Karhu follows the hotel's event calendar, Keloravintola is by reservation only apart from theme nights and ticketed dances, Punakettu, Rumpu Bar and Aarnikota publish theirs as dated periods, and Restaurant Aurora publishes no times at all. Check before you plan the evening around one.

pyha.name: Pyhä
pyha.title: Bars in Pyhä: Slope Pubs, a Fell-Top Wine Bar & Karaoke | LaplandBars
pyha.description: Where to drink in Pyhä: a slope pub beside the family slope, a wine bar on the summit and a year-round sports bar with karaoke. Hours and addresses.
pyha.tagline: Six bars around one resort, and the wine bar is at the top of the fell.
pyha.intro: Pyhä's six bars sit in Pyhätunturi. Two of them stand beside hotels: Mesta, a bar and terrace in the middle of the slopes next to Hotel Kultakero, and CAMP Kitchen & Bar PYHÄ at Kultakeronkatu 21 next to Hotel Pyhätunturi, where panoramic windows face the fells. On the same street, at number 4, Sport Bar Pyhä sits in the Pyhä shopping centre with a pool table, karaoke and Viaplay sports channels. Restaurant Huttuhippu is at Ukonhattu 1, beside the family slope, and its Huttu-Pub is credited with the resort's largest beer selection. Hanki Baari Pyhä is at Pohjoisrinteentie 1, at the foot of the North Slopes, and is closed until December 2026. The sixth is not at street level at all: Pyhä Dreams Wine Bar is in a cabin on the summit of Pyhätunturi, reached by the scenic lift.
know: Hanki Baari Pyhä at the foot of the North Slopes is closed and opens again in December 2026. When it runs, it is over-18s after 21:00 unless a parent is with you, and event nights are over-18 all evening.

Daily hours: Restaurant Huttuhippu 13–22, CAMP Kitchen & Bar PYHÄ 16–21 and Sport Bar Pyhä 17–24, which says it is open all year round. The other three, Mesta, Hanki Baari Pyhä and Pyhä Dreams Wine Bar, publish no set hours, so check with the venue.

Pyhä Dreams Wine Bar is at the top of the fell, up the scenic lift, and opens for a summer season and again for a winter season, so check the dates with the venue. Its guided tasting takes at most eight people, runs about two hours and does not include the lift ticket, so book ahead.

iso-syote.name: Iso-Syöte
iso-syote.title: Bars in Iso-Syöte: Slope Pub, After-Ski & a Summit Bar | LaplandBars
iso-syote.description: Where to drink in Iso-Syöte: a pub and hotel bar on Romekievarintie, an after-ski bistro by the back lifts, a summit restaurant. Addresses and menus.
iso-syote.tagline: There is no bar street here: every venue is attached to a hotel, a slope or a grocery shop, and two of the five sit on a fell top.
iso-syote.intro: Iso-Syöte's drinking is attached to its hotels, its slopes and one grocery shop, and the postal addresses read Syöte or Pudasjärvi. Two of the five sit on Romekievarintie at the foot of the front slopes: TunturiPUB at number 1, which shares premises with the Tunturi Market grocery shop and keeps board games in the corner, and Bistoria at number 4, the restaurant attached to KIDE Hotel, with wine by the glass from EUR 8.80. TunturiPUB stands a few dozen metres from the hotel, so those two are a short walk apart. Pärjä Ski Bistro is over on the back slopes at Takarinteentie 4, right next to the lifts, with a terrace that catches the spring evening sun. Ravintola Hilltop is higher again: 200 seats on the top floor of the Hilltop Hotel at the summit, the same room running as Cafe Hilltop from 10:30 to 18:00. Restaurant Kotva is on another fell, on top of Pikku-Syöte at Syötekeskuksentie 126, with three courses at EUR 59.
know: One of the five depends on the season. Restaurant Kotva serves dinner on Fridays and Saturdays only, in the autumn ruska season it announces, and the dates on its own page do not add up, so confirm them before you travel; at Ravintola Hilltop it is the menu rather than the venue that varies: its own site warns the a la carte can be limited outside winter and may depend on booking ahead.

TunturiPUB is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays, and the kitchen stops at 21:30 from Wednesday to Saturday even though the bar itself runs to midnight midweek and to 03:00 on Friday and Saturday. Pärjä Ski Bistro publishes its hours on Facebook only, not on its website.

Only TunturiPUB and Bistoria are neighbours: both are on Romekievarintie by KIDE Hotel, a few dozen metres apart. Ravintola Hilltop is at the summit of Iso-Syöte on Isosyötteentie and Restaurant Kotva on top of Pikku-Syöte, so each of those is its own trip up a fell rather than a walk from the slope base.

salla.name: Salla
salla.title: Bars in Salla: Ski Resort Pubs, Karaoke & Late Nights | LaplandBars
salla.description: Where to drink in Salla: two bars at the ski resort, a karaoke pub on Hautajärventie and a village pub in Vallovaara. Hours, addresses, what to check.
salla.tagline: Three of the four bars here run karaoke, and only one of those three is at the fell.
salla.intro: Salla splits two ways. Two of its bars are at the fell: Papana Pupi is the house pub of Sallatunturin Tuvat at Sallatunturi, Hangasjärventie 1, sharing a building with the reception and Restaurant Kiela, and its walls carry match jerseys and sticks from Finnish ice hockey players. Keloravintola, a log restaurant at Revontulentie 9, stands at the foot of the front slopes of Salla Ski Resort, fully licensed, with a sunny terrace and after-ski. The other two are Ravintola Sallan Maja and Evakko Pub. Sallan Maja, at Hautajärventie 32, runs a lunch and a la carte kitchen by day and its own pub, Majan Pubi, late, with karaoke, board games and a K-18 limit from 22:00. Evakko Pub is the pub at Kairalan Kievari in the village of Vallovaara, Vallovaarantie 209, in an old elementary school building, with darts and billiards in the game room.
know: Ravintola Sallan Maja's own pages disagree: its Finnish front page lists Mon-Thu 11–18, Fri 11–18 and again 22–04, and Sat 12–18 and again 22–02, while its English page says the pub is open Fri-Sat 21–04. Sunday is not in the hours block at all, and the Mon-Thu lunch buffet runs 11–14 at EUR 13.50 with salad buffet and coffee included.

Evakko Pub is in the village of Vallovaara, at Vallovaarantie 209. Its Fri-Sat 22–02 comes from a page whose content appears to date from 2018 and Visit Salla says only that the pub opens at weekends until the early hours when needed, so check before you set off; live music nights run to 03.

Keloravintola lists daily 13–20 and is open year round, and Papana Pupi runs on the Sallatunturin Tuvat banner, 08:00–22:00, later on winter gig nights but with no closing time published. Searching for Keloravintola also turns up a different one at Lapland Hotels Luostotunturi; the Salla one is at Revontulentie 9.
